list: The official 55 trophies, 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, 28 hidden, no online trophies. Names, descriptions and grades as PlayStation publishes them; guides in our own words.
sources_note: Unlock facts are drawn from the GTABase trophy guide and the PowerPyx trophy guide & roadmap, both cited beside every trophy. Where a guide says the exact steps are not yet confirmed, this guide says so instead of inventing them.

trophies.guide: The platinum is the reward for the other 54, so there is no separate task — it pops the moment the last trophy lands. PowerPyx puts the whole run at roughly 200 hours, most of it on the 100% checklist for A Long Road, so treat the platinum as a planning problem, not a grind: follow the roadmap in this guide (story first, 100% checklist second, questlines and stragglers last), keep cheats off — they disable trophies and saving — and let the checklist do the counting. One playthrough is enough; there are no difficulty settings and no online trophies.

steps: Play the story through all five chapters.
Finish the 100% checklist (A Long Road).
Clean up questlines, strangers and stragglers.
Keep cheats off for the whole run.

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is one of the first missions of Chapter 1, so this is a story trophy that arrives on its own — play the opening and it pops when the mission ends. GTABase lists it as unmissable, and there is no mission replay, so there is nothing to prepare and nothing to lose: just do not skip the opening missions. If you are tracking progress, this is the first of twelve story trophies; the other eleven are the four chapter trophies, the final mission, and the six named story missions.
trophies.missableReason: Story-gated: it only unlocks by completing the opening mission Gone Fishing. GTABase lists it as unmissable — play the opening and it pops — but it can only be earned at that point in the story, so do not skip the opening missions.

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 1. The trophy is awarded as Chapter 2 begins — GTABase notes it pops once you have played the first mission of Chapter 2, What's in the Bag? — so keep playing past the chapter's last mission and it will land. It cannot be missed. While you are in Chapter 1, do the one thing in the chapter that can be missed: the meditation flagged under Positive Mental Attitude, which GTABase and PowerPyx both call the game's only possibly missable trophy.

Chapter 2 is where the open world properly opens up: both characters are together after Coffee Break, which is when partner trophies, Bret's hunting quests and the final meditation spot become possible, so use the chapter to start the long counts (vehicle scans, meditations) rather than leaving them all for after the story.

trophies.guide: The hardest trophy: reach 100% completion, which the game tracks under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion once it appears after the story. The good news, per PowerPyx and GTABase, is that the checklist is lenient — closer to 60% true completion. It demands in full: every robbery (all 8 bank vaults and all 39 gang operations), all underwater discoveries, every Shooting Range gold medal, all drone races and all 15 of Bret's Target Decks. Everything else is partial: 100 optional missions, 200 of 277 vehicle scans, 100 of 255 animal studies, 15 of 18 meditations, 70 of 80 challenges, 300 stunts and 100 WAiNK scans. Anything you did during the story already counts. Budget around 100 hours for this stage alone.
trophies.name: A Long Road

steps: Finish the story, then open Progress > Stats > 100% Completion.
Clear the full requirements first: robberies, vaults, gang ops, ranges, drone races, Target Decks.
Work the partial counts: 200 vehicle scans, 100 animal studies, 15 meditations, 70 challenges, 300 stunts, 100 WAiNK scans.
The trophy pops when the checklist reads 100%.

trophies.guide: Complete any 250 stunts — the trophy needs 250, but the 100% checklist wants 300, so keep going past the pop. GTABase counts 397 stunts in total: 130 stunt jumps, 202 flights under bridges, 40 knife flights and 25 base jumps, in any mix, and the optional challenge on each stunt is not needed. Flying under bridges is the fastest way to build the count, and the map can show every Stunt Spot. Track the running total under Progress > Activities > Stunts.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once. GTABase lists them: fishing, hunting, golf, a shooting range, pool, basketball (sink one basket), an arcade game, winning a race (a car race, a race challenge or a Top Fun drone race) and a stunt. Progress > Activities shows what is left. Most of these happen naturally during the story and the 100% checklist, so treat this as a checklist to glance at rather than a grind — if one type is still missing late in the game, it is almost certainly golf or pool.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges, spread across 12 ranges — the silver trophy for marksmanship. GTABase notes the ranges also raise your Focus level, which helps with Gunslinger (5 takedowns in one Combat Focus). Take the challenges steadily rather than in one sitting: each range has its own set, and gold medals are the 100% checklist's requirement too, so this is one of the few trophies where the trophy and the checklist want exactly the same thing.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.

GTABase adds that the 100% checklist wants all 42 drone races, so while you are at a location, finish its remaining races there and then; coming back later costs more time than doing them in one visit. Drone races are a race activity, so a win here also counts toward the 'win a race' activity type for Master of None.

Fishing itself is also one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, so the first fishing trip does double duty.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy. Andy's quests are Lucia-only and start in Chapter 3, when he texts her an address in Belville. Do all five in order — Climbing the Cellerichain, Pay the Cellerica Fee, Peach!, Read the Label and Puff Puff Pass — and the last one awards the trophy. GTABase says the quests are still there after the story, but they are a character questline, so start them when Andy first texts rather than leaving the whole strand for the end.

trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat. It becomes possible once both characters are together, after Coffee Break in Chapter 2: call your partner (hold Right on the D-pad, then Triangle / Y), build a 4-star Wanted Level and escape — it only counts once you are out of the red heat zone. GTABase suggests the train tunnel north of Ambrosia in Kelly County for shaking off cops and helicopters, and notes bank vault robberies always give 4 stars, so this often unlocks during Maximum Withdrawal.

trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level. With your partner beside you, rob three shops in a row while you are still wanted (flashing red and blue). GTABase advises going in with body armor, sticky bombs and healing items, and notes the 3 jewelry stores in north Vice City — open after Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3 — are close together. The trophy can take about 30 seconds to appear after the third shop; if it does not, rob a fourth.

Stand next to a busy road and scan passing traffic, and scan everything you pass from the start of the game. The 100% checklist needs 200 base models out of 277, so this trophy is a milestone on a longer count; GTABase's vehicle list is the reference if you want to know which base models you are still missing.

trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus — click both sticks while aiming. Focus only lasts a few seconds, so fill it first (eat, drink or wash up at home; Adrenaline makes it last longer) and use an assault rifle. GTABase notes gang operation thugs work well, while cops, soldiers and civilians do not seem to count — so attempt it during a gang operation, where five thugs in one place are common, rather than during a random shootout.

trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA: steal one of the big passenger jets docked at a departure gate's boarding bridge — planes parked out on the airfield do not count — back it out, take off and get about 1 km away from the airport. GTABase names gates E3 and E4 as the easiest: drive through the airfield fence and use the door by the stairs next to the boarding bridge. The mission VCIA Takedown walks you through the airport first, so learn the layout there.

The description's line, 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos', is a joke about the Rhino tank; expect heavy resistance on the base, so go in with armor and a fast exit plan, and use the tank's cannon rather than its machine gun for the takedowns.

GTABase names Richardson Jewelry & Diamonds in Vice City as a store that works well. Patience is the whole method — one alarm and the trophy is gone for that attempt, so save first if you can.

Vaults open with the optional Chapter 4 mission That's Where The Money Is…: follow a security van to its bank and get into the vault while it is open. The haul is too heavy for one character, so hand a bag to your partner. Vaults always give 4 stars, so escape on a fast bike and then switch vehicles; each vault pays up to $205,000, and Yasmani sells van tips for $10,000 if you want the next one marked.

trophies.guide: Rob an Armored Truck and escape. The simplest route, per GTABase, is a bank vault robbery — it counts as long as you then escape the red heat zone or reach a Pay 'n' Spray. Before vaults are available, you can box in an armored truck, put a sticky bomb on its back doors, blow them open and get away. Either way the escape is part of the requirement: the trophy is about the getaway, not just the robbery, so plan your exit before you start.

trophies.guide: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. The alley is Kingpin Bowling in Port Gellhorn, a gang operation first marked by Hit Kingpin Bowling in Chapter 2. Take its three valuables: the luxury watch in the southeast office, the Gutterball Moreland 850 shotgun on the northeast table, and the safe in the northeast hallway (bring sticky bombs). The trophy pops once you lose the police — you do not need all three in one visit, but GTABase warns the robbery takes a long time to come back, so take everything in one run if you can.

trophies.guide: Choices made (for better or worse). The trophy tracks 500 actions that change your Criminal Profile — most players reach it without trying. Turn on Criminal Profile notifications in Settings > UI to watch the count climb. The warning matters more than the grind: GTABase and PowerPyx both stress that the Irredeemable criminal profile is permanent, so make your profile-changing choices deliberately and steer clear of the Irredeemable path — a choice you cannot undo.
